title: SLA-driven observability contracts for Dedicated inference pools
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that defines observability contracts tailored to Redwood Dedicated inference pools (reserved GPU capacity). The goal: make SLAs actionable through a compact set of metrics, spans, and dashboard panels so SRE, runtime, and customer success can agree on what "observability" means for a Dedicated customer and how to measure compliance against latency/availability SLAs and cost budgets.

Audience and Usage:
- SRE/ops oncall for Dedicated customers
- Serving-runtime engineers who own pool behavior and routing
- Solutions/CS for SLA reports and incident reviews
- Product for shaping guarantees and error budgets

High-level principles (short):
- SLA observability must be lightweight: ~10 primary signals per pool type + 2-3 trace anchors to root-cause high-latency/availability incidents.
- Signals must be actionable: each metric includes a remediation play (e.g., evict-queue, scale-up, route-fallback).
- Cost-awareness: every SLA panel includes a tokenized-cost lens so tradeoffs are visible to customers and internal teams.
- Deterministic naming: metric and span names must follow pool-scoped naming so dashboards can tile by customer/pool id.

Primary metrics (definitions, owner, instrumentation hints, initial alert proposal):
1) pool.p95_response_ms (unit: ms)
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - definition: 95th percentile request end-to-end latency measured at the pool ingress (includes routing + queuing + model-token time).
   - instrumentation: count+histogram at ingress with tags: pool_id, model_variant, tenant_id, request_type (chat|completion|embed).
   - alert (draft): p95 > 250ms for 5m AND p50 > 100ms -> severity: page.
   - remediation notes: check pool utilization, queue length (pool.queue_depth), KV cache-miss ratio; consider burst capacity or route fallback.

2) pool.availability_pct (unit: percent)
   - owner: eng-sre
   - definition: percent of successful responses (2xx) over total requests across pool nodes for a 1h window, excluding synthetic probes.
   - instrumentation: success/fail counters with error classification tags: infra_error, model_error, rate_limit, timeout.
   - alert (draft): availability < 99.9% over 1h -> severity: page.
   - remediation notes: verify node health, driver-level OOMs, model loading failures; see node-restart timeline.

3) pool.queue_depth (unit: integer)
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - definition: instantaneous length of request queue at schedulers for the pool (sum across schedulers).
   - instrumentation: gauge updated on enqueue/dequeue with pool_id, priority.
   - alert (draft): queue_depth > 200 sustained for 2m -> severity: page; queue_depth > 50 -> severity: ticket.
   - remediation: scale-up or enable burst, reduce per-request batch size, check for slow token paths.

4) pool.kv_cache_warmth_pct (unit: percent)
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - definition: fraction of requests served with a warm KV cache (prefix hit) during 5m windows.
   - instrumentation: tag per request kv_cache_hit=true/false; aggregate by pool_id and tenant cohort.
   - alert (draft): kv_cache_warmth_pct drops > 40% from baseline after deploy -> severity: ticket.
   - remediation: warm-up probes, preflight key replication, user-facing fallback policy.

5) pool.token_cost_per_1k (unit: USD per 1k tokens)
   - owner: finance/infra
   - definition: amortized infrastructure+model cost normalized per 1k tokens for the pool over 24h.
   - instrumentation: combine infra billing, GPU utilization, token emitted counters; surfaced as derived metric in dashboard.
   - alert (draft): cost rises > 25% week-over-week without matching traffic growth -> severity: ticket.
   - remediation: review quantization profile, batching configs, model variant routing.

Trace anchors and span design (naming conventions and trace stitching):
- Trace root: request.{pool_id}.{tenant_id}.root (logical root created at API ingress)
- Spans to include (minimum):
   - span.request.router (tags: route_decision, fallback_used)
   - span.request.scheduler (tags: queue_pos, queue_latency_ms)
   - span.request.model_infer (tags: model_id, quantized, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit)
   - span.request.kv_prefetch (tags: keys_requested, hit_ratio)
   - span.request.response_serialize (tags: payload_bytes)
- Trace sampling strategy:
   - Adaptive: keep 100% of spiky failures and top-1% latency outliers; sample 1% of normal traffic.
   - For Dedicated pools with paid SLAs: increase baseline sampling to 2–5% and keep a rolling reservoir per pool_id for postmortem.
- Linkage: all spans must carry pool_id, tenant_id, request_id, and a short routing fingerprint so traces can be correlated with metrics in dashboards.

Dashboard composition (minimum panels per pool tile):
- Left column: SLA lenses
  - p95/p99 latency timeseries (1h/6h/24h) with marker for SLA target
  - availability % (1h window) + synthetic probe status (last probe result)
  - recent incidents (last 7d) & error breakdown pie (infra/model/limit)
- Middle column: Capacity and health
  - pool.node_count, node_utilization (GPU%), queue_depth heatmap by minute
  - kv_cache_warmth by tenant cohort (bar)
  - node-level OOM/restart timeline
- Right column: Cost & configuration
  - token_cost_per_1k trend, batching size distribution, model_variant routing share
  - autoscaler decisions log (actions taken, scale delta)

Dashboard UX notes:
- Tile by pool_id at the top-level. Support drilldown to tenant_id and request_id using click-to-filter and a single click into the trace explorer.
- Default time window: 1h with quick presets: 6h, 24h, 7d.
- Panels must include runbook links and the last deploy hash so teams can quickly see correlation with rollouts.

Canary/rollout observability contract for Dedicated model/quantization changes:
- Before canary: snapshot baseline p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_warmth, queue_depth for target pool for the prior 7d.
- Canary probe set (synthetic + production): run a prioritized probe set at 5–10 RPS for 30m and collect full traces for failures/latency outliers.
- Acceptance gate (example): no increase in p95 > 10% and no increase in error rate > 0.05% for canary window; kv_cache_warmth delta <= 5%.
- If gate fails: automatic rollback + high-fidelity trace collection for 1h post-rollback.

Incident triage playbook (compact):
1) Identify signal: p95 spike OR availability dip OR sustained queue growth.
2) Immediate triage: open incident, set paging if page criteria hit, pin pool_id in incident summary.
3) Collect artifacts: timeline of node restarts, autoscaler logs, model load logs, top traces (latency outliers), tail-token-path heatmap.
4) First-remedy checklist (fast actions): route traffic to fallback pool, enable burst capacity, scale-up nodes, restart offending node.
5) Postmortem anchors: attach the baseline snapshot (7d), canary artifacts if rollout-related, decisions taken, and a degraded-customer impact spreadsheet.

Measuring SLA compliance and reports:
- Weekly SLA report per customer pool that includes: availability_1h_percentage, p95_last_30d, incidents_count_30d, cost_delta_vs_commit.
- Monthly trend deck for CS + finance showing cost/unit and action items for optimization.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Agree on exact SLA thresholds per tier (free/prod/enterprise) and export them into product SLA tables (Product to decide).
- Decide trace retention tiers for Dedicated customers vs hosted (cost impact). Proposal: Dedicated: 30d reservoir for pool-level traces, 90d for samples; Hosted: 7d reservoir.
- Implementation: add pool_id to all spans at ingress; confirm SDK changes in GITHUB-PR-9012.
- Cost metric ownership: finalize cost extraction pipeline (infra + model + amortization) with finance and infra by EOD-2025-03-12.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally opinionated to reduce metric noise while preserving investigatory power.
- Feedback requested on alert thresholds and sampling budgets. Please add comments inline or drop a reply to #obs-dedicated Slack.

Signed-off-by: Asha Patel (draft)
